requirements.requirement: Local logs on node1 persist and remain readable across a restart.
requirements.summary: A pre-restart marker was recorded in both journald and /var/log/messages. The node then underwent a bounded reboot: it was healthy beforehand, the connection was interrupted during reboot, its boot ID changed, logging services recovered, and the marker remained readable from the previous journal boot and the messages file. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the reboot.

requirements.requirement: Local logs are configured for a 14-day retention period.
requirements.summary: The effective journald configuration sets MaxRetentionSec=14day and daily journal segments. The rsyslog-managed files have daily rotation, 14 retained rotations, and maxage 14; logrotate parsed the policy successfully, and crond was active and enabled before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Logging has finite storage controls that prevent unbounded disk growth.
requirements.summary: Persistent journald is limited to 1 GiB while reserving 2 GiB free space, with 128 MiB journal files and a 256 MiB runtime fallback limit. Traditional local log files rotate daily or when checked above 100 MiB, retain only 14 rotations/14 days, and use compression. The live journal reported its effective 1 GiB maximum and passed integrity checks.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. node1 now uses persistent journald storage, applies coherent 14-day policies to journal and rsyslog files, and has explicit storage-growth controls. A complete reboot transition demonstrated a changed boot identity, recovered logging services, intact journals, and survival of pre-reboot log data. The provider-wide restart protocol was complete and consistent with the fixed lifecycle observations. Hygiene was strong apart from two small abandoned validation files in /tmp.
limitations: The evidence interval did not span 14 days or simulate sustained high-volume logging, so expiration and pressure behavior are inferred from the effective policies rather than observed over the full retention window.
Logrotate was validated in debug mode; an actual rotation and compression cycle was not captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: Chronological review found that the substantive mutations—writing the journald and logrotate policies, creating and labeling the persistent journal directory, restarting/flushing journald, writing bounded test markers, and scheduling the required reboot—were causally connected to configuration, activation, verification, or restart testing (cmd-4581c2fa8b504bfb, cmd-eac432ea074b43ad, cmd-641c8ddfe359491d, cmd-1fbd185863934ecf, cmd-11238db765564ac3, cmd-f0848eb1cbde4f84, cmd-1934467861cc4b08). No unrelated troubleshooting mutation was observed. The only unnecessary retained residue was /tmp/logrotate-debug.out and /tmp/logrotate-final-debug.out: they were created for validation by cmd-0025f2f73bd74350 and cmd-d3e8f93b9ac44f1e but remained after completion. This is minor, bounded residue. No failed services, new socket exposure, or package damage was observed; PID and system-private-directory changes were expected consequences of the reboot.
